adds.title: BOE-A-2017-5118 Ley 8/2017, de 7 de abril, integral del reconocimiento del derecho a la identidad y a la expresión de género en la Comunitat Valenciana. - BOE
adds.summary: Official gazette text of the Comunitat Valenciana's Ley 8/2017, de 7 de abril, integral del reconocimiento del derecho a la identidad y a la expresion de genero, published as BOE-A-2017-5118. Article 1 makes the law's purpose the guarantee of an adequate normative framework for gender self-determination for people whose felt gender identity differs from that assigned at birth, and public bodies of the Comunitat Valenciana must treat people according to their felt gender identity; Title III provides for administrative documentation and an advice-and-support service for trans people and their families. Primary legal text confirming the 'dedicated integral law on the right to identity and gender expression' this record cites, enacted 7 April 2017.

adds.title: BOE-A-2019-281 Ley 23/2018, de 29 de noviembre, de igualdad de las personas LGTBI. - BOE
adds.summary: Official gazette text of Ley 23/2018, de 29 de noviembre, de igualdad de las personas LGTBI (BOE-A-2019-281), the Comunitat Valenciana's general equality statute for LGTBI people. Its provisions cover non-discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity/expression, access and admission rights (art. 56), reversal of the burden of proof (art. 57), and a Title V regime of administrative infringements and sanctions (arts. 58-66) for discrimination against LGTBI people. Primary legal text confirming the community's general-LGTBI-statute category alongside its 2017 trans-specific law, the dual-category statutory framework on which this record's assessment rests.

adds.title: Seis meses de carcel por perseguir, insultar y grabar a una persona trans en Valencia - Observatorio de delitos de odio y discriminacion
adds.summary: Report of a conviction by the Audiencia Provincial de Valencia (Section 5) over a June 2022 incident in a Valencia park (Patraix), where an 18-year-old with several minors insulted, chased, recorded and mocked a trans woman solely because of her gender identity. The adult accepted six months' prison, suspended on condition of committing no offence for two years plus payment of a 720-euro fine and 1,000-euro moral-damages indemnity to the victim; two minors had already been sentenced to supervision measures, and the hate-crime prosecutor (fiscal coordinadora de delitos de odio) handled the case. Documents an institutional response channel operating in the community: a gender-identity-motivated offence investigated, charged and resulting in a court sentence in Valencia.

adds.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics, Nigeria, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
adds.summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note, June 2025, confirming the Sharia Penal Codes of the twelve northern states, including Bauchi, remain in force. The note records that a Sharia court in Bauchi sentenced three men to death by stoning for 'homosexual acts' in 2022 but that the sentence could not be carried out until ratified by the state governor, and that a further report placed a death-by-stoning sentence for homosexuality from a Sharia court in Bauchi in May 2024. It also records that at a sodomy trial in January 2014 at Bauchi's Tudun Alkali Upper Sharia Court an angry mob stormed the premises demanding a death sentence. This is the June 2025 government note the record cites for the code remaining in force and for the 2022 sentence having been pronounced but not executed.

adds.title: In Bauchi, 70-year-old Man, Two Others to Die by Stoning over Homosexuality - THISDAYLIVE
adds.summary: THISDAY, 3 July 2022: a Sharia court sitting in Ningi local government area of Bauchi State sentenced three men to death by stoning for homosexuality, among them 70-year-old Malam Haruna, based on Section 134 of the Bauchi State Penal Law of 2001. The prosecution was brought by members of the Hisbah Vanguard through Adamu Dan Kafi, who told the court the three were arrested committing the offence at Gwada village, Ningi LGA on 14 June 2022. Second national Nigerian paper confirming that Bauchi's Sharia court actually pronounced the stoning sentence this record is about.

adds.title: Homosexuality: How sharia court sentenced septuagenarian, others to death - Relatives | Punch Newspapers
adds.summary: Punch report of the 28 June 2022 Ningi Sharia Court death-by-stoning sentence against three men in Bauchi State, built on interviews with relatives, published 16 July 2022. It records that presiding Shariah judge Munka'ilu Sabo-Ningi held the men violated Section 134 of the Bauchi State Penal Law of 2001, that a 30-day appeal window was granted, and - through relatives of the convicted men - that the judgment had not been carried out at the time of reporting. Confirms both the pronouncement of the sentence and the absence of any execution on record that the summary relies on.

adds.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics, Nigeria, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
adds.summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note, June 2025, which singles out Kano among the twelve northern Sharia-code states. Its comparative table lists the Kano Sharia Penal Code (2000) as prescribing death by stoning for married or previously married men and 100 lashes with imprisonment for up to one year for unmarried men, and states that in Kano and Katsina the maximum penalty for 'lesbianism' is death while the other ten states punish it by flogging and up to six months' imprisonment. The note also records Kano-specific enforcement and gender-expression facts: eight people convicted of wearing female clothing at a wedding were reportedly flogged in public on the premises of the hisbah in Kano state in 2023, and Kano's separate Prostitution and Immoral Acts (Prohibition) Law criminalises cross-dressing by men. This is the June 2025 government note the record cites for the codes remaining in force and for Kano's capital maximum applying to same-sex acts between women as well as men.
